claims.quote: At every convenient place upon the line on either side of the Channel Tunnel there were enthusiastic spectators
claims.description: A railway tunnel under the English Channel links Britain and France, carrying troop trains.

claims.quote: the formation of an aerial park in this region, from which attacks could be made upon the vast industrial plant of the lower Rhine
claims.description: An air base is set up to launch bombing raids on the enemy's industrial region.

claims.quote: whose business it was to do what they were told by the mysterious intelligences at the direction of things in Paris, to which city the Whitehall staff had also been transferred.
claims.description: The British war staff moves to Paris under a single joint Allied command.

claims.quote: Upon these maps, as upon chessboards, Marshal Dubois, in consultation with General Viard and the Earl of Delhi, was to play the great game for world supremacy against the Central European powers.
claims.description: A great war for world supremacy is fought between France, Britain and Slav allies on one side and the Central European powers on the other.

claims.quote: But he had reckoned without a proper estimate either of the new strategy of aviation or of the possibilities of atomic energy that Holsten had opened for mankind.
claims.description: Atomic energy has been unlocked by a scientist and, together with air power, transforms warfare.

claims.quote: While he planned entrenchments and invasions and a frontier war, the Central European generalship was striking at the eyes and the brain.
claims.description: Air attacks target the enemy's command centers directly instead of fighting a frontier war (decapitation strikes).

claims.quote: She saw three black shapes swooping down through the torn clouds, and from a point a little below two of them, there had already started curling trails of red
claims.description: Enemy aircraft drop atomic bombs on Paris at night and destroy the Allied war headquarters.
claims.stated_time: on the night of July the second

claims.quote: the swift aeroplane, with its atomic engine as noiseless as a dancing sunbeam and its phosphorescent gyroscopic compass, flew like an arrow to the heart of the Central European hosts.
claims.description: An aeroplane is driven by a silent atomic engine.

claims.quote: Nearly overhead a German aeroplane was circling down from an immense height to challenge him.
claims.description: Defending aircraft patrol at high altitude, intercept intruding planes and fire on them in air-to-air combat.

claims.quote: The bomb flashed blinding scarlet in mid-air, and fell, a descending column of blaze eddying spirally in the midst of a whirlwind.
claims.description: A two-man aeroplane drops atomic bombs on Berlin, destroying the imperial headquarters.

claims.quote: Never before in the history of warfare had there been a continuing explosive; indeed, up to the middle of the twentieth century the only explosives known were combustibles whose explosiveness was due entirely to their instantaneousness
claims.description: Atomic bombs are invented that keep exploding continuously instead of going off in an instant.
claims.stated_time: the middle of the twentieth century

claims.quote: A little celluloid stud between the handles by which the bomb was lifted was arranged so as to be easily torn off and admit air to the inducive, which at once became active and set up radio-activity in the outer layer of the Carolinum sphere.
claims.description: The atomic bomb is a sphere of Carolinum coated with an inducive substance; tearing off a stud lets in air and starts a self-spreading radioactive chain.

claims.quote: Of all Hyslop’s artificial elements, Carolinum was the most heavily stored with energy and the most dangerous to make and handle.
claims.description: Scientists create artificial radioactive elements, one of which (Carolinum, half-life 17 days) stores enormous energy.

claims.quote: There, as more and more of the Carolinum became active, the bomb spread itself out into a monstrous cavern of fiery energy at the base of what became very speedily a miniature active volcano.
claims.description: A dropped atomic bomb bores into the ground and erupts like a volcano for weeks to years, flinging out radioactive debris.

claims.quote: to this day the battle-fields and bomb fields of that frantic time in human history are sprinkled with radiant matter, and so centres of inconvenient rays.
claims.description: Atomic bombing leaves battlefields contaminated with lingering radioactivity long afterward.

claims.quote: Certainly it seems now that nothing could have been more obvious to the people of the earlier twentieth century than the rapidity with which war was becoming impossible.
claims.description: Weapons grow so destructive that war itself becomes impossible.

claims.quote: Every sort of passive defence, armour, fortifications, and so forth, was being outmastered by this tremendous increase on the destructive side.
claims.description: Growing destructive power outstrips every kind of armor and fortification.

claims.quote: Destruction was becoming so facile that any little body of malcontents could use it; it was revolutionising the problems of police and internal rule.
claims.description: Small groups of malcontents gain city-wrecking power, changing policing and internal security (terrorism).

claims.quote: Before the last war began it was a matter of common knowledge that a man could carry about in a handbag an amount of latent energy sufficient to wreck half a city.
claims.description: A portable bomb small enough for a handbag can destroy half a city.

claims.quote: Collective civilisation, the ‘Modern State,’ was still in the womb of the future
claims.description: An organized collective civilization, the Modern State, will emerge after this era.
